_readme: The machine-readable form of the parity bands, plus the pins that
record where the port actually sits inside them. `gate.mjs` asserts this file
against a pair of dumps; nothing else in the tree may hold a second copy of
these numbers.
Two severities, and the difference matters:
BAND: the band itself. Zero tolerance on invariants, 1 ms on published
instants, 1e-9 on published degrees. A breach is a defect. A band
moves only with a written prediction first and Ishank's approval;
one has moved once, for the eclipse-table row.
PIN:  where the port measures *today*, far inside the band. A pin breach
is a review event, not necessarily a defect: a Node or Go bump can
move the last digits. Investigate, then re-pin deliberately and
write the delta down. `gate.mjs --allow-pin-drift`
downgrades pin breaches to notices while you are doing that; CI
never passes it.
`numericAbs` is applied to every numeric leaf, including the shadbala virupa
leaves (`*.total`, `*.sthana`, `*.dig`, `*.kala`) that have no row of their own.
That is the strictest existing band read onto leaves nothing else covers,
not a new one: those quantities run to O(500) virupas, so 1e-9
absolute is far tighter for them than for a degree.

provenance.measured: 2026-08-24; darwin/arm64 pins re-measured 2026-08-25 after the audit's FMA-barrier and typed-constant fixes
provenance.baseline: c38c606 plus the uncommitted src/ + tests/ working tree, with dasha.ts asOfDate applied

hosts.darwin/arm64: Apple M3 Max, node v24.4.1, go1.26.4, Ishank's machine, where every earlier recorded number was taken
hosts.linux/x64: Docker node:24-bookworm / golang:1.26 (node v24.19.0, go1.26.7) under --platform linux/amd64 on the same Apple silicon host, i.e. Rosetta-translated x86-64. IEEE semantics are preserved by translation, so these should equal native amd64, but that is an argument, not a measurement, and no native amd64 run has been made. Confirm on the first real CI run before treating these pins as blocking. STALE as of 2026-08-25: these numbers were measured before the audit barriered five astronomy products and typed the two FK5 constants, which tightened darwin by 2 leaves and ~450 changed values per stage. Expect linux to tighten similarly; the first native run must re-pin from the block the gate prints (it will report TIGHTENED, never a band breach).

provenance.bytesPinNote:
The document-byte pins have moved twice on 2026-08-29, both times with the delta predicted before it was measured, and neither time to make a failing check pass.
(1) -28 on every pin: the dump's `_meta` carried a key whose only content cited an internal planning document that does not ship. Removing it from both dumps removes a 28-byte JSON member.
(2) -243 at g2, -930 at g3, -1557 at full, identically on the TypeScript and the Go side: every em dash was removed from the library's own output strings (festival names, table descriptions, matching and dosha descriptions) and from the harness metadata. Each ' - ' written with an em dash is 5 bytes and became a 2-byte ': ' or ', ', so every replacement saves exactly 3 bytes. All three deltas are exact multiples of 3 (81, 310 and 519 replacements) and the TypeScript and Go deltas are equal to the byte, which is what says the two languages changed in lockstep. Every band held at 0 invariants and 0 shifted instants, and every non-byte pin (leaf counts, changed values, worst |delta|, worst leaf and path) was unchanged through both moves.
(3) 2026-09-24 audit fixes, full stage only, every move predicted per fix group and confirmed after the merge: TS +75966 and Go +75990 bytes. Brahma Muhurta moved to the 14th night muhurta, polar transition days now null, moonset no longer taken from the next day and one duplicate New York eclipse day removed (+74601 TS); Sankashti, post-adhika Ugadi and Navaratri, vriddha-trisprisha Smarta Ekadashi and adhika-year Onam added (+1815); Ashtottari and Yogini birth antardashas clipped, Narayan own-sign 12 years, a new pratyantarIn leaf (-1255); Nathonatha made continuous (-9); DST day walks and the Ekadashi year edge (+814). The numeric pins moved for the first time: numericLeaves 99 to 102 (three Shadbala leaves at e5-2088-reykjavik whose existing ULP-level Paksha difference now rounds differently against the new Nathonatha values, each at most 5.7e-14) and changedNumericValues 3141 to 3138 (+5 from those leaves, -8 from the removed duplicate eclipse's obscuration and magnitude leaves, which carried the known 1e-15 noise). The TS-to-Go byte gap went from 105 to 129 for the same two causes (+20 and +4). Every band held at 0 invariants and 0 shifted instants, and the worst numeric leaf and path are unchanged.
(4) 2026-09-24 reference-almanac festival rules, Yoni table and day convention, full stage only, predicted per group and confirmed after the merge: TS and Go each -22375 bytes, gap unchanged at 129, numeric pins unchanged. Tithi-day selection +4083 (holika_dahan added, duplicate vriddhi and kala days removed, days moved); nakshatra, solar and vara-in-month rules -25984 (Masik Karthigai duplicates removed, Onam once a year, karthigai_deepam added, vara rules in the purnimanta month); Pathu Porutham Yoni description -470; day convention 0 (same-width dates); -4 from JSON separators on days whose festival list both festival groups changed.
(5) 2026-09-24, the g2 and g3 pins, which (3) and (4) had left at their 5.3.0 values although three of the audit causes reach those stages. Attributed byte for byte against g2 and g3 dumps of the 5.3.0 tree, which reproduce the old pins exactly, with no residual: `specialYogas` under `computeEndTimes: false` (shape s2-narrow only) +81806, no next-day moonset -3724, the duplicate eclipse day -3257 TS and -3253 Go, and at g3 only the dasha clipping and pratyantarIn leaf -1255, the Pathu Porutham Yoni description -470 and Nathonatha -9 TS and +11 Go. g2: TS +74825, Go +74829, gap 90 to 94; g3: TS +73091, Go +73115, gap 111 to 135. Numeric pins move for the same causes as full: changedNumericValues 2264 to 2256 at g2 and 3046 to 3043 at g3, numericLeaves 97 to 100 at g3. Every band held at both stages. The same attribution run on full shows that the +74601 step in (3) is mostly `specialYogas` (+81806), not Brahma Muhurta, which moves values and no bytes.

_readme: The byte-identical gate the table band describes, over the
twelve table files `PARITY_STAGE=full` writes on each side.
Nine must be byte-identical. The three eclipse tables take an amended
row: byte-identical *except* `obscuration` and `magnitude`, which are the
only computed floats in any of the four formats and both end in the
platform's asin/sqrt, which can never be bit-identical. The gate
is that band's own wording: a masked comparison of every byte but those two
keys' digits, plus the numeric band on the digits.

_hostNote: The bands are host-independent; the pins are not. Both were measured, not assumed.
On linux/x64 every band holds exactly as on darwin/arm64: 0 invariants,
0 shifted instants, and the worst |Δ| is *bit-identical* on the two hosts
gate is fully host-stable too: the same 9 files byte-identical, the same 10
differing lines, and the same worst masked |Δ| to the last digit.
What moves is the *counts*, and the identity of the worst leaf at g2. That is why
`pins` is keyed by host. A host with no block here is not a failure: the gate
asserts the bands, prints the measured block to paste, and says so.
The cause is the platform, not the toolchain. Measured by running the TypeScript
dump on linux with node v24.4.1 (the exact version darwin uses) and getting
250723677, byte-identical to linux with node v24.19.0 and 3 bytes off darwin's
250723680. A Node patch bump did not move the document at all; changing OS and
architecture did.
The two builds differ from each other by very different amounts. TS arm64 vs TS
amd64 at g2: 1 leaf, 14 changed values, worst 5.684e-14. Go arm64 vs Go amd64 at
g2: 4 leaves, worst 1.705e-13, over 2102 `sun.siderealLongitude` and 1780
`moon.siderealLongitude` values. So the Go build is markedly less
architecture-stable than V8 is, and `sun.siderealLongitude` matches the
TypeScript exactly on arm64 while differing on amd64. docs/porting.md §1.1's FMA
barriers are the obvious suspect and an unbarriered site the obvious lead, but
no site has been named yet.
